title: decision: rewrite the day's commit messages and force-push, once
description:
Mark, 2026-11-26, after the commit-message review. Recorded because it
overrides a standing rule in AGENTS.md.

## The rule it overrides

AGENTS.md: "Push only with Mark's explicit OK. If a push is rejected,
stop and report it. Never `pull --rebase`, reset or force-push."

Mark asked for the rewrite knowing it is a history rewrite, was shown
the costs, and chose the full scope. The rule stands for every other
case; this is one authorised exception, not a new practice.

## What was done

All 32 commits of 2026-11-25/26 (a0c92bc2..HEAD) had their messages
rewritten, under one rule in Mark's words: "commit messages do not need
to explain what the code does, the code explains what the code does."
So anything the diff shows was cut, and what survives is why, what it
costs, a constraint from outside the code, and a bug the diff does not
reveal.

Mechanism: `git filter-branch --msg-filter`, keyed on the original
commit hash. `git rebase -i` is unavailable in this environment, and
filter-repo is not installed. A backup branch
`backup/pre-message-rewrite-20261126-1009` holds the pre-rewrite
history.

## The costs accepted

- 25 of the 32 were already pushed to a public repository, so main was
  force-pushed. Anyone holding a clone or fork of those 25 has a
  history that no longer matches.
- Commit hashes changed, so bead citations of the form "Done in
  <hash>" had to be rewritten. 14 beads cited the pushed commits and 3
  cited the unpushed ones.

## Why not the narrower option

Rewriting only the 7 unpushed commits would have needed no force-push
and broken nothing, and the three habits are already rules in AGENTS.md
so new messages come out clean either way. Mark chose the full scope
anyway: the 25 pushed messages are the ones the review found worst, and
the repository is his.
close_reason: Recorded. The rewrite and force-push were done 2026-11-26 and the bead is the record of the AGENTS.md exception.
